title: Maps from an ideal power lift modulo principal maps over a flat neighbourhood
statement: Let R and S be commutative rings and S an R-algebra with flat structure map. Let I be a finitely generated ideal of R such that R/I -> S/IS is an isomorphism, let n >= 1, and let N be an R-module. For every R-linear map d : I^n -> S tensor_R N, there exist an R-linear map l : I^n -> N and m in S tensor_R N such that 1 tensor l(r) = d(r) + r m for every r in I^n. Scalar extension is as in [def-weil-module-base-change] and flatness as in [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map].

proof.text: Put J = I^n and choose finitely many generators f_i (adjoin zero if necessary). Form F = R^t, W generated by f_i e_j - f_j e_i, M = F/W, and mu : M -> R sending e_i to f_i, with image J. Its kernel K is killed by J: for z = sum a_i e_i in K, f_j z = sum a_i f_i e_j = 0. Evaluating d : J -> S tensor N on f_i gives a cycle x whose induced map from the scalar-extended M kills the scalar-extended K.

Let Z(P) be the cycles f_i x_j = f_j x_i and B(P) the principal cycles (f_i p). H(P) = Z(P)/B(P) is killed by J: f_i x is the boundary with parameter x_i. Write Z as the kernel of the finite matrix of differences and B as the image of P -> Z. Tensor finite-product comparison, flat tensor exactness and tensor right exactness identify S tensor H(N) with H(S tensor N), sending 1 tensor [y] to [1 tensor y]. Since J kills H(N) and n >= 1, the torsion-module comparison makes H(N) -> H(S tensor N) bijective. Lift [x] to [y]. Equality of classes gives m with 1 tensor y_i = x_i + f_i m.

The cycle y induces yhat : M -> N. Tensoring the presentation of M and the kernel sequence of mu identifies their base changes with the corresponding objects for f_i over S. The tensor of yhat on K is zero: the map defined by x kills K, and the correction (f_i m) factors through mu, hence also kills K. As J K = 0, the Hom comparison for torsion sources is injective, so yhat vanishes on K already over R.

Factor yhat through M/K = J to get l : J -> N. On each generator, 1 tensor l(f_i) = d(f_i) + f_i m. Both sides are R-linear in the element of J, so the equality holds on their span J. For J = 0 the conclusion is vacuous; for J = R, d is principal and l = 0, m = -d(1) works.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_ideal_power_hom_lift
    {R : Type u} {S : Type v} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
    (_hflat : (algebraMap R S).Flat) (I : Ideal R) (_hI : I.FG)
    (_hquot : Function.Bijective
      (Ideal.quotientMap (I.map (algebraMap R S)) (algebraMap R S) Ideal.le_comap_map))
    (n : ℕ) (_hn : 1 ≤ n)
    {N : Type w} [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N]
    (d : ↥(I ^ n) →ₗ[R] S ⊗[R] N) :
    ∃ (l : ↥(I ^ n) →ₗ[R] N) (m : S ⊗[R] N),
      ∀ r : ↥(I ^ n), 1 ⊗ₜ[R] l r = d r + (r : R) • m
